The Four Thick Ropes: Dismantling the Feudal-Patriarchal System
Peasant
Political Power
Political Authority (The State/Landlord)
The backbone of all other systems. Overthrowing
the rural monarchs and the armed forces of the
landlords is the prerequisite.
Clan Authority (The Temple/Elders)
The system ranging from the central ancestral
temple down to the head of the household.
Religious Authority (The Gods/Superstition)
The supernatural system. Once political power is
seized, the peasants themselves repurpose temples
and cast aside idols.
Masculine Authority (The Husband)
Domination over women. Weakened as the rural
economy shifts and women organize into associations.

The "Movement of the Riffraff" is the Vanguard of the Revolution
The Gentry's View
"It's Terrible!"
The reactionary view of peasants
creating terror, acting "unruly,"
turning things upside down, and
going too far.
The Revolutionary View
"It's Fine!"
This violence is the necessary
overthrow of a thousands-year-old
autocratic system. Proper limits
have to be exceeded in order to
right a wrong.
The Core Insight: The Poor Peasants (70% of the rural population) have nothing to lose.
Without the poor peasants (the 'riffraff'), it would be impossible to overthrow the local tyrants.
A revolution is not a dinner party; it is an act of violence by which one class overthrows another.

The Economic Imperative: Defeating the White Blockade
State
Enterprise
Handling essential commodities directly
(importing salt and cloth, exporting grain and
wolfram) to bypass merchant profiteering.
Co-operative
Enterprise
Growing rapidly via consumer, grain,
and producer cooperatives funded
by mass-subscribed economic
construction bonds.
Private
Enterprise
Promoted and encouraged within legal
limits; essential to the interests of the
state and people at the present stage.
Key Insight
Dispensing with economic construction does not 'subordinate everything to the
war effort"-it weakens the war effort by starving it of material prerequisites.

The Strategist's Ultimate Weapon
The Communist Party's strategy was not built on superior firepower, but on
the precise, ruthless application of sociological analysis, ideological
discipline, and the weaponization of the masses' daily needs.
Revolution is not a spontaneous event; it is a meticulously engineered system.
